FLOCCULUS: A small lobe in the under surface of the cerebellum, near the middle peduncle; the subpeduncular lobe.
FORFEITER: One who incurs a penalty of forfeiture.
FLEETEN: Fleeted or skimmed milk. [Obs.] Fleeten face, a face of the color of fleeten, i. e., blanched; hence, a coward. "You know where you are, you fleeten face." Beau. & Fl.
FALLOPIAN: Pertaining to, or discovered by, Fallopius; as, the Fallopian tubes or oviducts, the ducts or canals which conduct the ova from the ovaries to the uterus.
FELDSPAR: A name given to a group of minerals, closely related in crystalline form, and all silicates of alumina with either potash, soda, lime, or, in one case, baryta. An organ of a fish, consisting of a membrane supported by rays, or little bony or cartilaginous ossicles, and serving to balance and propel it in the water. Greenleaf.
FULL-SAILED: Having all its sails set,; hence, without restriction or reservation. Massinger.
FINBACK: Any whale of the genera Sibbaldius, Balænoptera, and allied genera, of the family Balænopteridæ, characterized by a prominent fin on the back. The common finbacks of the New England coast are Sibbaldius tectirostris and S. tuberosus.
FREMITUS: Palpable vibration or thrill; as, the rhonchial fremitus.

FLABBY: Yielding to the touch, and easily moved or shaken; hanging loose by its own weight; wanting firmness; flaccid; as, flabby flesh.
FLYBANE: A kind of catchfly of the genus Silene; also, a poisonous mushroom (Agaricus muscarius); fly agaric.
FLY-BITTEN: Marked by, or as if by, the bite of flies. Shak.
FETID: Having an offensive smell; stinking. Most putrefactions . . . smell either fetid or moldy. Bacon.

Detached works, depending solely on their own strength, belong to the class of works termed forts. Farrow.

FEWNESS: 1. The state of being few; smallness of number; paucity. Shak. 2. Brevity; conciseness. [Obs.] Shak.
FABACEOUS: Having the nature of a bean; like a bean.
FOREBY: Near; hard by; along; past. See Forby. Spenser.

FOOT POUND: A unit of energy, or work, being equal to the work done in raising one pound avoirdupois against the force of gravity the height of one foot.
FULGURATION: 1. The act of lightening. [R.] Donne. 2. (Assaying) The sudden brightening of a fused globule of gold or silver, when the last film of the oxide of lead or copper leaves its surface; -- also called blick. A phenomenon called, by the old chemists, fulguration. Ure.

FRIGIDARIUM: The cooling room of the Roman thermæ, furnished with a cold bath.
FOUNDLING: A deserted or exposed infant; a child found without a parent or owner. Foundling hospital, a hospital for foundlings.
FERULIC: Pertaining to, or derived from, asafetida (Ferula asafoetida); as, ferulic acid. [Written also ferulaic.]
FOZINESS: The state of being fozy; spiritlessness; dullness. [Scot.] [The Whigs'] foziness can no longer be concealed. Blackwood's.
FAGGING: Laborious drudgery; esp., the acting as a drudge for another at an English school.
FLEME: To banish; to drive out; to expel. [Obs.] "Appetite flemeth discretion." Chaucer.
FULL-BLOOMED: Like a perfect blossom. "Full-bloomed lips." Crashaw.
FLATLY: In a flat manner; evenly; horizontally; without spirit; dully; frigidly; peremptori;y; positively, plainly. "He flatly refused his aid." Sir P. Sidney. He that does the works of religion slowly, flatly, and without appetite. Jer. Taylor.
FOLIOLE: One of the distinct parts of a compound leaf; a leaflet.
FUSAIN: (a) Fine charcoal of willow wood, used as a drawing implement. (b) A drawing made with it. See Charcoal, n. 2, and Charcoal drawing, under Charcoal.

FRUTESCENT: Somewhat shrubby in character; imperfectly shrubby, as the American species of Wistaria.
FURUNCLE: A superficial, inflammatory tumor, suppurating with a central core; a boil.
FISHFUL: Abounding with fish. [R.] "My fishful pond." R. Carew.
FORESTAGE: (a) A duty or tribute payable to the king's foresters. (b) A service paid by foresters to the king.
FEROCITY: Savage wildness or fierceness; fury; cruelty; as, ferocity of countenance. The pride and ferocity of a Highland chief. Macaulay.

FILEFISH: Any plectognath fish of the genera Monacanthus, Alutera, balistes, and allied genera; -- so called on account of the roughly granulated skin, which is sometimes used in place of sandpaper.
FATIMITE: Descended from Fatima, the daughter and only child of Mohammed. -- n. A descendant of Fatima.
FARMING: Pertaining to agriculture; devoted to, adapted to, or engaged in, farming; as, farming tools; farming land; a farming community. The business of cultivating land.
FLUSTRATION: The act of flustrating; confusion; flurry. [Colloq.] Richardson.
FLIRTATION: 1. Playing at courtship; coquerty. The flirtations and jealousies of our ball rooms. Macaulay.
FLUORESCIN: A colorless, amorphous substance which is produced by the reduction of fluoresceïn, and from which the latter may be formed by oxidation.

FIMBLE: Light summer hemp, that bears no seed.

FLATFISH: Any fish of the family Pleuronectidæ; esp., the winter flounder (Pleuronectes Americanus). The flatfishes have the body flattened, swim on the side, and have eyes on one side, as the flounder, turbot, and halibut. See Flounder.

Pan through the pastures oftentimes hath run To pluck the speckled foxgloves from their stem. W. Browne.
FRIBORGH: The pledge and tithing, afterwards called by the Normans frankpledge. See Frankpledge. [Written also friburgh and fribourg.] Burril.

FLAMBOYANT: Characterized by waving or flamelike curves, as in the tracery of windows, etc.; -- said of the later (15th century) French Gothic style.
FEUILLETON: A part of a French newspaper (usually the bottom of the page), devoted to light literature, criticism, etc.; also, the article or tale itself, thus printed.
FATHERLINESS: The qualities of a father; parantal kindness, care, etc.

FRUTEX: A plant having a woody, durable stem, but less than a tree; a shrub.

FADEDLY: In a faded manner. A dull room fadedly furnished. Dickens.
FELLOW-FEELING: 1. Sympathy; a like feeling. 2. Joint interest. [Obs.] Arbuthnot.

FERIAL: Same as Feria. 1. Of or pertaining to holidays. [Obs.] J. Gregory. 2. Belonging to any week day, esp. to a day that is neither a festival nor a fast.

FRINGE TREE: A small oleaceous tree (Chionanthus virginica), of the southern United States, having clusters of white flowers with slender petals. It is often cultivated.
FIGURAL: 1. Represented by figure or delineation; consisting of figures; as, figural ornaments. Sir T. Browne. 2. (Mus.) Figurate. See Figurate. Figural numbers. See Figurate numbers, under Figurate.
FLUORIC: Pertaining to, obtained from, or containing, fluorine.

FIRMLESS: 1. Detached from substance. [Obs.] Does passion still the firmless mind control Pope. 2. Infirm; unstable. "Firmless sands." Sylvester.

FRIGHTFULLY: In a frightful manner; to a frightful dagree.
FATHERLY: 1. Like a father in affection and care; paternal; tender; protecting; careful. You have showed a tender, fatherly regard. Shak. 2. Of or pertaining to a father.

FORESTICK: Front stick of a hearth fire.

FANTIQUE: State of worry or excitment; fidget; ill humor. [Prov. Eng.] Dickens.
FLABELLINERVED: Having many nerves diverging radiately from the base; -- said of a leaf.
FUNCTIONLESS: Destitute of function, or of an appropriate organ. Darwin.

FLAMBOYER: A name given in the East and West Indies to certain trees with brilliant blossoms, probably species of Cæsalpinia.
FREEBORN: Born free; not born in vasssalage; inheriting freedom.
FREE-SWIMMING: Swimming in the open sea; -- said of certain marine animals.

FORELAY: 1. To lay down beforehand. These grounds being forelaid and understood. Mede. 2. To waylay. See Forlay. [Obs.]
FRONTED: Formed with a front; drawn up in line. "Fronted brigades." Milton.
